parsed.explanation: Recent structural positives: 2020 decriminalisation plus criminalised sexual-orientation discrimination (a working-lever removal and a statutory recourse tool), no trans-specific entry rules, growing NGO infrastructure, and a visible trans public figure. Negatives: no gender-marker change (largely resident-facing, light weight), a documented 2024 police attack on a trans woman with arbitrary detention and degrading treatment — a state-actor incident, though a single case, with no custody-placement information and under-investigated violence per the 2024 shadow report; formal protections 'not matched by practice'. No documented social-acceptance tradition balances the friction. Thin-data jurisdiction: I extrapolate from the reform trajectory and dead-letter-free criminalisation toward moderate safety, tempered by the state-perpetrated custody incident and unquantified violence. Sits between the 0.55 profiles (partial remedies, scattered state friction) and 0.65; the unremedied police-custody element pulls it toward the lower figure.
